issues.legal_issue: Theft amounts to robbery only when the offender voluntarily causes or attempts to cause death, hurt, wrongful restraint, or fear of such harm for the purpose of committing the theft or carrying away the stolen property.
The allegations in the FIR did not disclose the ingredients of dacoity under Section 395 of the Indian Penal Code.

A criminal-intimidation offence requires a threat made with intent to cause alarm or to compel or prevent conduct, while an offence of intentional insult requires abusive words or conduct likely to provoke a breach of the peace.
The FIR’s allegation that abusive language was used, without stating the words or otherwise establishing intentional insult, did not disclose an offence under Section 504 of the Indian Penal Code.
A court considering quashing an FIR on grounds of frivolity, vexatiousness, or ulterior motive must examine relevant attending circumstances and investigation materials beyond the FIR’s averments.
Delay in lodging an FIR, by itself, is not a ground for quashing, but delay combined with circumstances making the prosecution case inherently improbable may justify quashing.

An accused’s criminal antecedents cannot, by themselves, justify refusing to quash criminal proceedings where the FIR fails to disclose an offence or the case falls within the established quashing parameters.
The criminal proceedings could be quashed where the vague and delayed allegations, considered with the attending circumstances, rendered their continuation an abuse of process.
